## Chapter Sixteen

Cleaning Up



The two bikes sat in a field as the riders knelt over the grass with the old map folded out in front of them. “So maybe we should have gone left at the big mountain thingy” Rolle said pointing out something on the map. Lucas squinted at it “That’s not a mountain, that’s a dam” he finished shooting an accusing look at his friend. “Dude, we are so lost” Lucas finished and sat back, his knees starting to hurt from being on them for so long examining the map. Lucas surveyed the area, the long fields that had once, long ago probably been used for raising crops now only supplied crab grass to whatever animals would eat it.

In the distance, lines of tall pine and oak trees made a wall showing where the field ended in all directions. The air was cold but still tonight and the suits kept them surprisingly warm while on the bikes. He watched as the sun made its final trip of the day down towards the tree line. Turning to Rolle he motioned towards the horizon “We don’t have a lot of time; can you figure out where we are going?” he asked with urgency in his tone.

“Ha, got it” Rolle said in triumph folding the map carefully as the folding lines had long ago begun to come apart. They mounted the bikes and Rolle took the lead, Lucas felt the wind as it buffeted the suite and the knot in his stomach as he lifted off the ground totally open to the environment. But even with the fear there was exhilarating at being closer to nature, being closer to the experience of driving. He had not realized until that moment what he had been missing. There was something raw and visceral about riding a bike and he found he rather enjoyed it, despite the situation and the dire nature of their mission a smile spread across his face as he accelerated to keep up with his friend.

They flew low over the trees keeping out of the normal skyway and away from the sparse traffic this far out. The earth still had not recovered from its loss of population and nowhere was more evident than the further you got from the cities. The country was spread out most of the old towns now abandoned or there population so low they might as well be.

Lucas watched as small towns that dotted the forests and plains below came and went. Some of them still maintained and others crumbling as nature had begun the process of reclaiming the space once inhabited by humans.

After a while Lucas was lost in his thoughts, the drone of the engine and the green landscape lulling him and allowing his mind to drift. He thought about Dyson, the man who saved him, his teachings and his way of pushing him, He remembered how he talked about the underground and the conviction and love for this thing that Lucas now found himself was absolute it was firm faith and belief, he couldn’t imagine him turning. It was inconceivable he thought. The voice of his old master coming to him “But everyone has a breaking point” it whispered Lucas found it Ironic that the voice arguing against him was Dyson’s own. But no, Lucas had learned many things from Dyson, he was now a walking weapon, an encyclopedia of tactics and war but the most important thing he had learned from Dyson, was conviction and loyalty. Somehow, they had altered the tape, he hoped, he just prayed Victoria found out how.

Rolle banked and began to descend pulling Lucas out of his thoughts as he mimicked the motion following him. In the distance he could see an old farmhouse fast approaching. Two ancient and rusting silos silhouetted the landscape behind the old two-story craftsman that from the looks of it, had stood for the better part of a century.  The bikes descended Rolle circling the property and Lucas in pursuit as they canvased the property for anything out of the ordinary. Lucas didn’t know if the security forces had received all the property names or just the key ones, but so far everything seemed normal here. The bikes landed behind the house about twenty feet from the rear door. Lucas could see forms as they looked out the window and then opened the door coming out onto the porch Lucas couls see the silouettes of figures as they carefully approached, trying to decide if they were friend or foe.

The sun had set, and darkness had set in, Lucas flipped on the low light setting on the helmet, the world washing over in grey as the figures resolved showing him more detail as they approached. A man and a woman, the man carrying what looked like a baseball bat and the woman unarmed. “Who are you?” The small man asked with a country drawl, one that Lucas did not recognize. But he could hear the suspicious resonate in those words. Rolle getting off the sleek black bike and walking to within ten feet of the couple. Lucas could see the man tense, his hands tightening on the old wooden bat. “Ask me the code” Rolle said dispassionately, not taking off the helmet giving the two a very ominous presence to the two-farm couple.

The man thought for a moment, apparently trying to remember one of the codes that would authenticate the two as members of the underground. Finally, he spoke urgently. “What’s the last business in the universe?” he asked. Lucas took a step forward causing the man and woman to take a step back. “A Diner” Lucas said and could see the two deflate with relief. “What are you guys doing here?” the woman asked relieved and no longer afraid but there was still an edge to her voice. Rolle studied the tree line Lucas could see the light from the helmet, he had turned on his low light mode so chiding himself for focusing on the two and not on the possible dangers that could be approaching he continued the conversation. “We have been compromised, this is a scorched earth, we need to get you guys moving to the rendezvous” he said and waited for his words to sink in.



“Wha-What happened?” the man asked his face showing worry, the details clear in Lucas’s low light helmet view. “We don’t have time” he said “We need to get moving, now” he said, then focused on the tree line as well, he wasn’t sure anyone would move on this location, but they were here to ensure everyone got out.

“I need you to move, get anything you need to take and let’s get you out of here, we need to hurry” Lucas prodded as the two stood there dumbfounded, he could understand they were well removed from the day to day of both the government and the underground and had probably never thought this day would happen. At his urging they jumped into action, heading back into the house. Lucas turned on his mic in the helmet, after a moment of digital noise the secure connection was established to Rolle. “I will go around and secure the front” he whispered so his friend could hear. The helmet was clear enough so the person speaking sounded like he was directly over the other persons shoulder. Rolle nodded, never taking his eyes off of the field and the silo’s.

Leaving the bike Lucas walked around to the front of the house, keeping his eyes outward as he scanned any movement on the horizon. Reaching up he turned the enhanced audio up listening for any unusual noises, aside from the rustling from within the house there was nothing. Something had the hairs on the back of his neck standing on end. He couldn’t put his finger on it but something wasn’t right. After a bit of listening it hit him like a ton of bricks, there was no noise coming from the forest, no creatures rustled, nothing moved or cried out. It was completely dead. Something in the woods had sent the animals to ground and that usually meant only one of two things, a predator or man.

He heard the front door open and just as the couple came out of the house carrying boxes, the second floor turned into a fireball, Lucas was thrown ten feet as his visor dimmed to protect his eye. The blue fireball sent splinters of wood and metal out in all directions turning the second floor of the old farmhouse into a 360-degree claymore. To his horror Lucas’s visor dimmed turning over he came face to face with the female occupant of the house, her face a mask of horror. A giant wooden support had pierced her mid-section pinning her to the ground in her final moments.

Lucas stood sluggishly, unsteady on his feed, he surveyed the carnage that had only moments ago been the peaceful yard of a country farm. Small fires were everywhere, The man had not been as lucky as his wife, he had been sheared in two, part of him , the top part lay with his face towards the house, giving Lucas a full view of the inside of his cranial cavity.

He forced back the urge to vomit, trying to assess the threat. He turned, looking for Rolle but not able to see him or the bikes from his current position. Instead he turned to see the line of troops emerging from the tree line in front of him.

Thankfully the house was still ablaze, the sun that they had created where the house had stood only a moment ago was shielding him from there sensors. He turned and ran at full speed, dodging to avoid fires and large chunks of debris. He had almost made it around the house when the first of the bullets zipped by his helmet and a second one grazed his arm, causing a tight burning sensation over his bicep. He couldn’t stop, to stop would be to die. He turned once he cleared the side of the house, now Lucas could see Rolle lying unconscious on the ground.

“Don’t be dead dammit” he whispered as much of a prayer as a curse. He slid the final few steps on his knees over to his friend. Turning him over Rolle groaned and began to try and get up. “We have to go NOW” he screamed at his friend. Rolle was going to slow, but with Lucas’s help he managed to get him to his feet. There was no way he could pilot the bike. Pulling his friend along with his arm over his shoulder, Lucas mounted his bike and after a few moments, coaxed his friend on the back.

He could trust him to hold on in his condition, reaching around Rolle he felt around for what seemed like an eternity to get into the pack the other man was wearing. He knew it had to be there, he kept his eye on the corner of the house, knowing if he saw the troops emerge, they would be dead before they could escape. He did his best to control his breathing Feeling around inside the pack. After a million years, his hands closed over the item he so desperately sought and pulled the long black nylon rope out of the pack. Quickly he threw it over his head as if he were about to jump rope and synch it around, he and Rolle, then tied his hands together around his waist.

He started the Bike and cursed, waiting for the red blinking light, willing it to turn green as the bike powered itself. The light turned green and Lucas slammed his right foot on the pedal, lifting the bike quickly ten feet in the air. Turning the throttle, he banked 180 degrees, feeling Rolle shift but before he could slide off, Lucas righted the bike and then tweaked the throttle as far as it would go , rocketing towards the tree line in the distance, knowing the only protection he would have from the troops and their guns was the safety of the trees.

It approached quickly, but before he could reach it, tracer rounds like angry fireflies buzzed past him. He slalomed the bike trying to make the bike a more difficult target. He felt more then saw the bullet as it sparked off the cowling along the right side of the bike. Then they were in the trees. Turning his head slightly giving his one good eye as much of a frontal view as he could, he dodged tree after tree, scaping along one, the leg guard the only thing keeping his leg from disintegrating on the trees ample trunk. Forcing himself to calm down and bringing himself back from the brink of panic, he forced his hand to back off the throttle and slowing the bike enough to be able to navigate the tight trees.

Lucas could still hear rounds as they slammed into the trees behind him, but unless the troops got lucky, then they were safe.

Lucas began to raise the bike above the tree line when suddenly a spotlight lit up the ground around him, and gun shots began to pepper the trees and ground around the bike. Cursing he hadn’t realized that they had them at a tactical disadvantage, they could go invisible with the suits, but the Bike because of the electronics was like a beacon, shining bright in a forest devoid of any electromagnetic emissions.

he accelerated, trying to get ahead of the light, but whatever was above them was also above the tree line and could move faster and safe then the two of them on the bike, and now with the twice the weight, the acceleration of the bike and the maneuverability was hampered. He thought desperately for anything he could do, and no avenue of escape existed, they were sitting ducks, just waiting for one of those marksmen to get a bead on them and blow them out of the sky.

They were dead, and he knew it. He narrowly missed another tree almost careening off a second one. His mind desperately trying to think of a solution. Rolle grumbled behind him “Sorry buddy, I fucked up good, and now we are dead” he said his voice thick with remorse and guilt. “Middle button” the slurred voice in his helmet whispered. Lucas cocked his head “What?” he asked, thinking Rolle was just speaking nonsense, and maybe that was a good thing, maybe his last moments on this earth would be mercifully clouded to the danger they now faced. And then he repeated it “Middle Button” and Lucas felt the tugging of the rope as Rolle tried to move his bound hand. Lucas looked down and now noticed the three buttons just under the speedometer on the bike. “What the hell” he thought, thinking it couldn’t get much worse than this. Slammed his hand on the middle button and held his breath.

A moment later the back of the bike lit up as metals balls four inches in diameter launched from behind the seat straight up in the air, Lucas could only make this out through the rearview mirror glances as he continued to dodge trees. The world lit up with a Blue incandescent light above them and Rolle, using the last of his energy said, “Bank NOW” and then slumped against his friend, passed out and only sitting on the bike because of the binds that tied them.

Lucas didn’t hesitate and banked hard right. Goosing the accelerator, the forest opened into a field, allowing him to gain even more speed, no longer did the spotlight follow them and the sound of the whirring engine was. Growing fainter behind them. He dared bring himself just above the tree line and continued to fly, tops of trees and long branches reaching for the sky slapping his legs and the bottom of the bike. After twenty minutes, Lucas banked in a random direction, Still refusing to lessen the bike’s acceleration.

After forty minutes a red light appeared on the console and the bike began to decelerate and lower towards the earth. Something had broken in the bike finally and it was now starting to die.

Lucas brought the vehicle in for a landing, five feet off the ground the bike finally died, dropping them to the ground, the bike and riders separating as they slid across the soft wet earth. Lucas and Rolle still tied together lay there for what seemed an eternity. Finally, Lucas stirred, untying himself from his friend and pulling the pack off of Rolle’s back.

He gently dragged his friend into the underbrush of another tree line and then bringing some loose branches over, he did his best to cover the dead hover bike. Lucas spent an hour making his friend comfortable and tending to his wounds. Amazingly enough aside from the cuts and bruises, he was in decent shape.

Sometime after the sun had risen and rose into the middle of the sky Rolle finally stirred awake, coming to with a start. Lucas gently held his friend done. “Calm down, we are safe man” he said trying to soothe his friend. His own relief at not being alone second only to the fact that his friend had rejoined the living. Rolle leaned back, wincing in pain, his helmet lying next to him, Lucas had pulled it off soon after settling him into the brush.

“Where are we” Rolle cracked, trying to clear his parched throat. Lucas came to sit next to his friend. Gently cradling his head, he slowly fed his friend water. Rolle gulped greedily at the small sips, finally indicating he was finished, Lucas lowered his friends head and put the cap on the bottle of water. “Where are we” he asked again, this time sounding better. Lucas looked around for the hundredth time as if this time surveying his surroundings would give him a clue as to their location. “I have no idea, the bike is dead, and there are no landmarks to tell me where we are, besides. I can’t read the map for shit” he said smiling sheepishly. Rolle chuckled, the action making him wince with pain. “Hand me the backpack” he said motioning for the black bag out of reach. Lucas retrieved it and brought it over to his friend. “hey, I have to ask, what the hell was the middle button on the bike?” Rolle, looked confused, his eyes unfocused as he tried to resolve the comment and then the light of understanding hit.



“Oh, I guess we had company then?” he asked more of a statement through then a question Lucas just nodded. “A little addition to the Bike from V, it shoots balls filled with light radioactive isotopes and a few other things that disrupt electronic sensors for a few minutes. Lucas nodded now understand how it was they were spared at the last moment of their life.

Rolle rolled to lean on his side, digging into the bag, he retrieved a radio and the map, arching his eyes at Lucas “You didn’t try to call for help?” he asked Lucas smiled and shrugged “You had the codes and I didn’t want to draw attention” highlighting though he had serious training, there were areas that he severely lacked. Rolle just nodded. Understanding that any random calls could have summoned the wrong kind of help.

Rolle began to fumble with the dials on the radio, wincing every so often, reminding them both of his delicate condition. Unfolding the ancient map, he entered in a frequency into the old digital radio from memory. “We have hidden relay’s out from our safe houses back towards DC, which should allow me to reach, as long as we didn’t get too far from the safehouse” he said, turning dials on the radio and listening intently. After a few minutes a pre-recorded message, a string of seemingly random numbers emitted from the speaker.  Lucas cocked his head listening to the numbers “What the hell is that?” he asked as the numbers stopped and started again, the set repeating.

“Numbers Station” Rolle said and then Lucas got it, he had read of the old school way ro relay messages, though because of the ability of the Cerberus system to easily decode most encryptions why they would dare using those he wondered. Rolle seemed to anticipate the question. “Most of the time, it’s simply random numbers, however in case of emergency short pre-designated messages or number strings can be sent to all stations. The computer can’t really decode them because the numbers themselves are the messages” he said Lucas now understanding. They had resurrected the old method of communications with a new twist.

Rolle slowly stepped through a few frequencies and then keyed the mic “Mama Bear, this is Falcon, we have a broken wing over” he un keyed the mic and listened. He resent the same message a few more times until a familiar voice professional though sounding relieved “Acknowledged” Aunt Sally’s deep Boston Baritone stated and then the airwaves went dead.

Rolle turned the radio off and laid back down, all energy he had saved resting had just been expended.
